claim: A June 2026 arXiv paper (within recency window) quantifies plain cosine-similarity RAG serving stale facts: 'The central result is the stale-fact-error rate: when required to answer, RAG serves superseded values 15-40% of the time; MemStrata drives this to ~0%, a failure class RAG cannot avoid.' MemStrata is a 'deterministic supersession layer' -- i.e. explicit versioning/supersession metadata rather than similarity ranking alone -- which is direct evidence for why freshness has to be tracked as metadata, not inferred from embeddings. claim: MCP (spec revision 2026-07-28, within recency window) is the closest thing to an open, cross-vendor standard touching retrieval, but it standardizes generic resource discovery/read (resources/list, resources/read, a URI, mimeType, and annotations including a lastModified timestamp) -- it defines no retrieval-specific request shape (no query field, no similarity score, no ranked-result-set schema) and no schema for describing a knowledge collection/corpus as a unit. This is evidence for the open question, not a standard retrieval-result schema itself.

claim: A January 2026 arXiv paper states directly that there is no standard interface across vector databases: 'Divergent Naming Conventions and Operations: Fundamental operations have inconsistent names. Corrected 2026-09-09: this text lives in the full HTML paper body (https://arxiv.org/html/2601.06727), not the abstract, and the genuine text retains the numbered citation markers [6][7][8] that the previous snippet had silently dropped.
